programme: CDX1 acting upstream of the posterior HOX patterning genes HOXB4 and HOXB9, alongside the oncofetal stemness factor SALL4 (which shares hematopoietic/epithelial stem-programme targets such as ABCG2, BMI1, NANOG, SOX2, ZEB1, EPCAM with CDX1's own CDH1/CLDN targets) — a developmental hematopoietic/vascular-progenitor specification axis that is redeployed as a stemness programme in adult tissue
role_in_a: Not documented in this record. The physiological expectation from this axis's known biology is progenitor-cell specification (HOXB4 is the classic hematopoietic stem-cell self-renewal factor and has been used to expand endothelial progenitor cells), which would matter for vascular repair/neovascularisation after ischaemic injury — but this is inference from the factors' general biology, not a role attested for cardiovascular disease here.
role_in_b: SALL4 is the one factor with an actual signal in the record (top ~5th percentile of Open Targets scores for clear cell renal carcinoma), consistent with its documented role as an oncofetal stemness/EMT driver reactivated in several carcinomas; its target set (ABCG2, ZEB1, NANOG, SOX2, BMI1) is the signature of a drug-resistant, progenitor-like tumour subpopulation. HOXB9's angiogenic/invasion targets (VEGFA, FGF2, CXCL8) and CDX1's epithelial targets could plausibly support the same phenotype, but neither has an Open Targets association with this cancer.
shared_axis: Both diseases can in principle recruit an embryonic hematopoietic/vascular-progenitor specification programme — physiologically for vascular repair in cardiovascular disease, pathologically as a stemness/EMT programme in tumour subpopulations in ccRCC — but the record supplied does not show this bridge being drawn for this specific pair; it is a mechanistic hypothesis built from the factors' known individual biology, not a documented connection.
reasoning: CDX1-HOXB4/B9-SALL4 is a real, nameable developmental programme, but the evidentiary record for this pair is almost empty: Open Targets shows no cardiovascular association for any of the twelve factors, CDX1 and HOXB4/HOXB9 show no or only marginal (0.19, 0.03) ccRCC association, and only SALL4 shows a strong one. No papers in the retrieved material could be confirmed as discussing any of these factors in either disease, so the account rests on background knowledge of the factors rather than on anything retrieved.
support: none found — no PMIDs are given in the supplied material for this pair; the papers referenced for SALL4, APEX1 and HOXB9 are noted only as unjudgeable or off-topic, with no identifiers provided.
how_to_falsify: Knock down SALL4 (with and without CDX1/HOXB4 co-depletion) in a ccRCC line and check whether the ABCG2+/CD133+ stem-like fraction and ZEB1-driven EMT markers actually drop; separately, overexpress HOXB4 in patient-derived endothelial progenitor cells and test whether it fails to improve neovascularisation in an ischaemic vascular-repair assay. If neither manipulation moves the relevant phenotype, the shared-axis account is wrong.
caveats: Only 4 independent cohort pairs underlie the 120 patient-group comparisons, and blood and kidney are mechanistically distant tissues. The tissue-generic exclusion list already stripped out the obvious blood-lineage regulators (KLF1, CEBPD, GFI1B, PBX1, JUNB, TBX21, PRDM1, CIITA), so the twelve factors that remain are enriched for less-expected, harder-to-interpret hits rather than canonical blood/vascular biology. HAND2, the single highest-recurrence factor (76/120), has no Open Targets or paper support for either disease and does not integrate into the named programme — it is flagged here rather than folded into the story. Eight of the twelve listed factors (HAND2, COPS5, ZNF335, ZFP64, APEX1, NFIL3, MAML2, FOXN1) span unrelated biology (cardiac/neural-crest development, COP9 signalosome, chromatin/neurodevelopment, DNA-repair/redox, circadian/immune regulation, Notch coactivation, thymic epithelium) and were left out of carrying_factors because they do not fit any single coherent module with the others.
